segments.text: New York City passed Local Law 144, requiring companies to audit their AI hiring tools for bias. Illinois passed BIPA for biometric data. Colorado passed an AI Act requiring disclosures. Europe is further ahead with its own AI Act. But these are patches on a system that has no fabric. The vast majority of Americans have no legal protection against algorithmic discrimination.

scenes.scene_name: Official screening report revealing stranger's evi

segments.text: She requested her screening report, as is her legal right. And what she found was someone else's eviction on her file. A stranger's debt, merged with her identity because of a similar name and a shared zip code. A database ghost. She disputed it. Thirty days later, the error was removed. She got the apartment.

segments.text: But here's what Diane did that almost nobody does. She kept going. She filed a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. She posted her screening report online, with the errors circled. It went viral — not because her story was unusual... but because she had the receipts. Thousands of people in her comments saying the same thing: this happened to me. I didn't know I could check. I didn't know I could fight it.

segments.text: You are being scored right now. By companies you have never heard of, using data you never gave them, feeding algorithms you will never see. Those scores are deciding where you can live, where you can work, what medical care you receive, and how much you pay for the roof over your head. They are doing this at scale, at speed... and in the dark.
